title: AVL right rotation with a grandchild
summary: Rotate unbalanced node 5 right, promoting its left child 3 to root. Reattach the former right child of 3, node 4, as the left child of 5.
context: Root 5 has left child 3 and right child 6; 3 has left child 1 and right child 4; 1 has only left child 0. The unbalanced node 5 is labeled node, its left child 3 is child, and the right child of 3, node 4, is grand_child.

The balance factor is left subtree height minus right subtree height. An empty subtree has height −1 and a leaf 0. The links give root 5 a left height of 2 and a right height of 0, so its factor is 2 and a right rotation is needed.
description: The right rotation promotes left child 3 to subtree root and moves the old root 5 to its right. Since the right child of 3 was grandchild 4, save its reference first and reattach it as the left child of 5. Because 3 < 4 < 5, node 4 stays in the right subtree of 3 and to the left of 5, preserving search tree order.
First save grand_child = child.right, then set child.right = node, and finally node.left = grand_child. Node 1 with its left child 0 remains to the left of 3. Node 6 remains the right child of 5.

Three panels, left to right: before rotation, after the right rotation and transfer of the grandchild, and the tidied layout. The middle panel already shows all final links. The pale dashed old positions of 5 and 6 and their old links provide a reference. The last panel removes the dashes and adjusts the layout without rotating again.
result: All nodes are retained. The inorder sequence remains [0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6].

frames.title: AVL right rotation with a grandchild
frames.explanation: After rotation, both subtrees of new root 3 have height 1, restoring balance. Nodes 0, 4, and 6 remain leaves.

steps.title: Locate grandchild 4 for reattachment
steps.explanation: Before rotation: Root 5 has left child 3 and right child 6; 3 has left child 1 and right child 4; 1 has only left child 0. Nodes 0, 4, and 6 are leaves. Here node=5, child=3, and grand_child=4. The left and right heights of the root are 2 and 0, giving balance factor 2. Save the reference to grandchild 4 before rotating right.
steps.key_state: Before rotation: Root 5 has left child 3 and right child 6; 3 has left child 1 and right child 4; 1 has only left child 0. Grandchild 4 awaits reattachment.
steps.announcement: Identify unbalanced node 5 and grandchild 4 to reattach.

steps.title: Rotate right and reattach node 4
steps.explanation: Right rotation complete. Root 3 has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has only left child 0; 5 has left child 4 and right child 6. Nodes 0, 4, and 6 are leaves. Node 3 has risen to root and 5 occupies its former right child position. Since 3<4<5, grandchild 4 reattaches to the left of 5. Dashed former positions of 5 and 6 and their old links show the original layout. There are still 6 actual nodes.
steps.key_state: After the right rotation: Root 3 has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has only left child 0; 5 has left child 4 and right child 6. All current links are in place. Dashes mark former positions only.
steps.announcement: Complete the right rotation, attaching grandchild 4 to the left of 5.

steps.title: Show the balanced tree
steps.explanation: The old dashes disappear and the layout is tidied. No further rotation or reference changes occur. Root 3 has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has only left child 0; 5 has left child 4 and right child 6. Nodes 0, 4, and 6 are leaves. Both subtrees of root 3 have height 1. Inorder traversal gives [0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6].
steps.key_state: Dashes removed; no second rotation. Root 3 has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has only left child 0; 5 has left child 4 and right child 6. Both subtrees of the new root have height 1.
steps.announcement: Remove the dashed reference marks to show the balanced subtree.
